Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring state contracts be performed by citizens.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to requiring state contracts be performed bycitizens of the United States or persons authorized by federal law towork in the United States; amending RCW 43.19.1932; adding a newsection to chapter 28B.10 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 39.04RCW; adding a new section to chapter 47.28 RCW; creating new sections;and declaring an emergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: It is essential thatthe legislature and state agencies spend tax dollars in a manner thatis both responsible and consistent with the economic interests of thestate and the nation. The legislature and state agencies should,therefore, consider indirect benefits that may be achieved whenentering into contracts for public works, personal services, purchasedservices, information services, and highway design and construction.Such benefits include, but are not limited to, job creation, capitalinvestment, and economic stimulus.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28B.10 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: All work under a public works, personalservices, purchased services, or information services contract that isentered into by the state under this chapter, or under any subcontractawarded under such a contract, must be performed by citizens of theUnited States or persons authorized by federal law to work in theUnited States.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 39.04 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: All work under a public works contract that isentered into by the state under this chapter, or under any subcontractawarded under such a contract, must be performed by citizens of theUnited States or persons authorized by federal law to work in theUnited States.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.19.1932 and 1989 c 185 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, thedepartment of corrections shall be exempt from the following provisionsof this chapter in respect to goods or services purchased or soldpursuant to the operation of correctional industries: RCW 43.19.180,43.19.190, 43.19.1901, 43.19.1905, 43.19.1906, 43.19.1908, 43.19.1911,43.19.1913, 43.19.1915, 43.19.1917, 43.19.1919, 43.19.1921, 43.19.1925,and 43.19.200. (2) All work under a public works, personal services, purchasedservices, or information services contract that is entered into by thedepartment of corrections, or under any subcontract awarded under sucha contract, must be performed by citizens of the United States orpersons authorized by federal law to work in the United States.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 47.28 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: All work under a public works,personal services, purchased services, information services, or highwaydesign and construction contract that is entered into by the stateunder this chapter, or under any subcontract awarded under such acontract, must be performed by citizens of the United States or personsauthorized by federal law to work in the United States.

If any provision of this actor its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to otherpersons or circumstances is not affected.

If any part of thisact is found to be in conflict with federal requirements that are aprescribed condition to the allocation of federal funds to the state,the conflicting part of this act is inoperative solely to the extent ofthe conflict and with respect to the agencies directly affected, andthis finding does not affect the operation of the remainder of this actin its application to the agencies concerned. Rules adopted under thisact must meet federal requirements that are a necessary condition tothe receipt of federal funds by the state.
Captions used in this act are notany part of the law.
This act shall not apply tocontracts entered into before July 1, 2005.
This act is necessary forthe immediate preservation of the public peace, health, or safety, orsupport of the state government and its existing public institutions,and takes effect immediately.
